scenes.voice: Mars. The fourth planet from the Sun. It has captivated human imagination for centuries — and we are finally close enough to touch it.
scenes.visual: Wide cinematic view of Mars from orbit

scenes.text:
Its surface is covered
in iron oxide.
scenes.voice: Its entire surface is coated in iron oxide — rust. That is what gives Mars its signature red glow, visible even from Earth with the naked eye.
scenes.visual: Close-up of rusty Martian rocks and soil

scenes.text:
Mars once had oceans.
And maybe life.
scenes.voice: Scientists believe Mars once had vast liquid oceans. Ancient river valleys and lake beds suggest it may have harbored the conditions for microbial life billions of years ago.
scenes.visual: Ancient Martian landscape with dried riverbeds

scenes.text:
Humans are going to Mars.
This decade.
scenes.voice: And now humans are planning to set foot on Mars within this decade. The dream that once lived only in science fiction is becoming an engineering reality.
scenes.visual: Astronaut stepping onto the Martian surface at sunrise
